name: from_raw_in
declaration: unsafe fn from_raw_in (ptr : * const T , alloc : A) -> Self
rules: For Rc<T, A>::from_raw_in(ptr, alloc) to be safe, ptr must have been returned by Rc<U, A>::into_raw.
For Rc<T, A>::from_raw_in(ptr, alloc) to be safe, if ptr was returned by Rc<U, A>::into_raw and U is sized, U must have the same size and alignment as T.
For Rc<T, A>::from_raw_in(ptr, alloc) to be safe, if ptr was returned by Rc<U, A>::into_raw and U is unsized, U's data pointer must have the same size and alignment as T.

For Rc<T, A>::from_raw_in(ptr, alloc) to be safe, if U or U's data pointer is not T but has the same size and alignment, the reinterpretation must satisfy reference-transmutation validity requirements: the reinterpreted reference must be valid at both its source and destination types.
For Rc<T, A>::from_raw_in(ptr, alloc) to be safe, ptr must point to a block of memory allocated by alloc.
The caller of Rc<T, A>::from_raw_in(ptr, alloc) must ensure that a specific value of T is dropped at most once, even if the returned Rc<T, A> is never accessed.
